mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over the past 3 months compresses discount rates for equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward 5-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods where FEDFUNDS declines by at least 0.5% over the prior 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 4.5% signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of months where UNRATE exceeds 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate a broad-based demand contraction that triggers a sell-off in equities, leading to negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods where both HOUST and RSAFS decline by at least 1% from prior month values.

mechanism_narrative: In periods of high industrial production growth (INDPRO growth > 2% annually), the S&P 500 exhibits positive forward returns as manufacturing strength supports corporate earnings, but this effect reverses when growth slows below 1%.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods where INDPRO growth exceeds 2% annually.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) signals strengthening labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of months where PAYEMS increases by at least 100k from prior month.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly housing starts (HOUST) below 1700 thousand units indicates a weakening housing market that reduces consumer confidence and corporate investment, causing negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of months where HOUST falls below 1700.0.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in inflation (CPIAUCSL) and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signal a monetary tightening cycle that increases real interest rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods where both CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS increase by at least 0.2% and 0.1% respectively from prior month.

mechanism_narrative: In periods of strong GDP growth (GDPC1 annualized growth > 2%), the S&P 500 exhibits positive forward returns as economic expansion supports corporate earnings, but this effect weakens during recessions.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of quarters where GDPC1 annualized growth exceeds 2%.
